text:
Alex: FYI quickstart sample app triggered a refresh-storm over the weekend 10s 429s. Looks like token refresh retries bypassed our client limiter.
Maria: I noticed a customer report that matched this pattern. Did you see token churn aligned with the spike?
Alex: Yes, token expiry window + parallel refresh retries = burst. Our per-connection limiter in JS doesn't protect the refresh path.
Jon: Go SDK uses a single global bucket which prevented the worst of it. JS per-conn buckets are the issue.
Sasha: My quick investigation: refresh requests call into the request layer before the shared adapter limiter. We should route refresh through the same shared limiter or queue.
Maria: Two mitigation ideas: 1) serialize refreshes with a small queue and jitter, 2) expose an SDK flag to prefer serialized refresh affinity for multi-conn apps.
Jon: Also consider capping concurrent refreshes to 3 by default instead of 5. When many clients spawn, that multiplies.
Alex: I've got a repro script that opens 100 sockets and forces expiry, will attach gist.
Sasha: Patch idea: add SharedLeakyBucket in adapter and ensure refresh acquires token from it. Example pseudo:
```
const shared = new SharedLeakyBucket({tokensPerSec: 300, burst: 50})
client.on('refresh', async () => {
  await shared.acquire(1)
  await sleep(jitter(20,150))
  return doRefresh()
})
```
Jon: Circuit breaker tuning too 1s current breaker trips too fast during refresh surges. Proposed: threshold 6 fails / 1s window, cooldown 3s.
Maria: Telemetry note: sample high-frequency 429s so we don't OOM observability. Use event sampling for repeat errors (sample_rate=0.05) but keep unique errors unsampled.
Sasha: I'll open a PR with tests that simulate concurrent refreshes and assert no >5% 429 rate under default sampleapp config.
ci-bot: [CI] job/refresh-throttle-shared-limiter started #704 :gear:
Alex: Immediate patch for quickstart: set tokenRefresh: "serialized" and reduce burst to 20. Can we roll that to canary?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled at 03:00 UTC.
Jon: Long-term: server could send x-client-rate-hint header with quota guidance. SDK can adapt local windows to that header.
Maria: +1, reduces client/server mismatch. Also docs: add migration notes and recommended settings for multi-conn sample apps.
Alex: Action items: Sasha PR (shared limiter + tests), Maria telemetry sampler + docs, Jon rate-hint design. I'll update quickstart now and monitor. :thumbsup:
